_comment: Canonical proper nouns for Defenders of the Realm. Copied VERBATIM from narrative-bible.md and src/content/story.ts. Do not paraphrase. These names are shared by the React v1 engine and the Unity v2 port.
theHeartTagline: The living core of Elarion — if it falls, the village falls.
_guardianLegacyNote: Retired title — the player is now 'the Keeper' (STORYLINE.md §4). Preserved so any v1 data reference does not hard-error.
_bossSyndrathNote: Apex village wave-boss (the Black Dragon). NOT from narrative-bible.md / story.ts — agent-authored content the owner pulled in and ratified 2026-05-19 (see docs/port-notes/dragon-boss.md §1). Keyed here as a proper noun so the HUD / boss bar never hardcodes it; the displayed name can be re-pointed without touching code.
heartWingDescription: Elarion's airborne aspect; Elarion sometimes walks the sky and the Folk call it the Heart-Wing.
tunnelOrigin: made by the Heart's own roots
_tunnelNameNote: WO-1044 R1/R2, owner ruling 2026-08-17 ('yes to all defaults on 1044'). RETIRED: 'The Hollow Roads'. That name read as THE HOLLOWED'S roads, which promises enemies inside a graph that deliberately authors zero encounters (nine rooms, no traps, no keys, no chests) -- so the player walked an empty crossroads and concluded content was missing. 'The Rootways' explains the quiet as lore: the Heart's song runs down there, so the rot does not; and it explains why the tunnel reaches exactly the four marches, because roots reach where the wards are. THE ID IS DELIBERATELY NOT RENAMED: the scene/graph id stays 'dg_hollow_roads' (BiomeRoads.TunnelSceneId), a contract shared by BiomeRoads.ArmRoomIdFor, dg_hollow_roads.json (dual copy), HollowRoadsDropInjector and BiomeRoadsRegression. Ids are live contracts; display names are not. Pinned by BiomeRoadsRegression Case 7, which fails both if this key drifts from BiomeRoads.TunnelDisplayName and if the retired name returns.
_regionNamesNote: WO-1044 R3, owner ruling 2026-08-17. Code said 'Stoneback'/'Ashwood' while narrative canon said 'Stoneback Ridge'/'Corrupted Ashwood'; the two disagreed. RULED: the SHORT forms are the UI names (they fit the travel prompt, 'Travel to Ashwood (deadly)'), and the LONG forms are PROSE ONLY -- narrative docs, region intro voice lines, quest text. The RUNTIME authority is ZoneManager.Regions, never this file: these keys are the canon RECORD so the ruling has a home outside a markdown doc, and BiomeRoadsRegression Case 3 fails if the short forms here ever drift from that table.
bibleTitleTagline: Tend the Heart. Hold the dark.
_taglineLegacyNote: SUPERSEDED 2026-07-24 (owner directive, Pets→Echoes rebrand) — the single canonical title tagline is now 'Echoes of a Forgotten Civilization' (the Echoes are the awakened essences of the people the Heart of Elarion once guarded); tagline AND titleTagline both carry it so whichever the UI reads is correct. The prior tagline 'Hold the line' (WO-570) plus the earlier 'Hold the Chord. Defend the Spire.', 'Hold the chord. Hold the dark.', and bibleTitleTagline 'Tend the Heart. Hold the dark.' plus the Spire/Chord/Lantern/Stone-Choir motifs are RETIRED; bibleTitleTagline is kept here as a historical reference only.
_gameSubtitleNote: Updated 2026-06-28 (WO-570). gameTitle is the MAIN game title 'Echoes of Elarion'; gameSubtitle 'Defenders of the Realm' is the SERIES/franchise label — this game is a chapter of the Defenders of the Realm saga (full title 'Defenders of the Realm: Echoes of Elarion'). The intro video bakes both on-screen.
_gameSubtitleLegacy: RETIRED subtitles: 'Defenders of the Realm: Elarion', 'Defenders of the Realm: The Lantern of Avalon'.
_selaLegacyNote: Sela Thornquiver is the v1 archer name — superseded by Nessa (STORYLINE.md §4) in the v2 Stone Choir pivot. Retained here so old save/data references do not hard-error.
_garranLegacyNote: WO-861 A0 (owner ruling 2026-08-02): the Knight's canonical name is GROM. The key stays 'garran' so old save/data references do not hard-error (same pattern as _selaLegacyNote above); only the player-facing VALUE changed. en.json hero.knight.name already reads Grom.
_namesNotInSources: Bryn, Mara, Tovin, Eira, Aelf, Mira were requested by the task brief but do NOT appear in narrative-bible.md or story.ts. Placeholder values mirror the requested spelling; verify against canon before shipping. See canon-data.md.
_firstLightNote: narrative-bible.md uses 'the First Light' as the planter(s) of Elarion. No standalone 'First Light' event term was found in the sources; value here matches the requested wording but is unverified. See canon-data.md.
_upgradeQueueNote: WO-1045. The building upgrade button's QUEUE-FULL face. ASCII only (TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu). These are the only NEW words that WO authored: the refusal SENTENCES it shows come live from BuildTimerService.LineFullMessage / TryBuySlot and are deliberately NOT duplicated here — two copies of a refusal is the drift bug the WO closes. upgradeQueueFullDetail's {0}/{1} are DEPTH (items lined up, queueDepthPerLine=5); upgradeQueueCrews' {0}/{1} are CONCURRENCY (jobs running at once, freeBuildSlots=2). Never swap those: exhausted concurrency QUEUES, only exhausted depth REFUSES, and the remedies differ.
_upgradeShortfallNote: WO-1037. The building upgrade button's MISSING-RESOURCES face - the shortfall band (dead state + harvest path on the wider half, ONE impulse-pack offer on the narrower one). ASCII only (TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu). upgradeShortDetail {0}=units still needed, {1}=resource word; upgradeShortHarvest {0}=resource word, lowercased by the View - it is FIRST and on the WIDER half on purpose (WO-1037 section 1: the harvest path stays first-class, the pack is the alternative, never the recommended route). upgradeShortPackOffer {0}=pack name, {1}=amount granted, {2}=resource word, {3}=USD reference price; its embedded newline splits the pack's NAME from its NUMBERS so neither has to be truncated on the narrow plate. upgradeShortPackSoon is the INERT plate's own label: the offer cannot purchase (FeatureFlags.RealmStorePurchase is off AND this surface has no purchase route at all - WO-1037 section 2 / WO-931), and its only action is to dismiss for that upgrade this session. Do NOT reword it into a Buy call-to-action while the plate is inert - a CTA over a rail that cannot transact is precisely the WO-931 defect this ticket was written to avoid repeating.
upgradeShortHarvest: Harvest more {0}, or set an Echo to gather it.
_redeemNote: WO promo-redeem door. The Realm Store's Redeem-a-Code screen (RedeemCodePanel) and every failure sentence PromoCodeService can raise. ASCII only (TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu). EVERY failure says what happened AND whether the code was spent - a bare 'invalid code' on a redeem screen reads as a scam, which is why each server error gets its OWN sentence and none of them is reused. redeemSuccess {0}=the reward summary composed from redeemRewardCrystals/redeemRewardCoins. This entry is DELIBERATELY not gated on FeatureFlags.RealmStorePurchase - that flag gates BUYING, not redeeming.
redeemBlurb: Have a code from an event, a creator or the team? Enter it here.
redeemSuccess: Code accepted - {0} added to your realm.
redeemSuccessNoReward: Code accepted, but it carried no reward to add.
redeemErrInvalid: We do not recognize that code. Check the spelling and try again - nothing was used up.
redeemErrAlreadyUsed: You have already redeemed this code. Each code can be used once per player.
redeemErrExpired: This code has expired and is no longer being accepted.
redeemErrPlayerLimit: You have reached the promo code limit for this account, so no more codes can be redeemed.
redeemErrOffline: We could not reach the rewards server. Your code was NOT used - check your connection and try again.
redeemErrIdentity: We could not verify your account, so the code was NOT used. Sign in, then try again.
redeemErrSignIn: Sign in before redeeming a code - rewards are tied to your account.
redeemErrUnknown: Something went wrong on our end and the code was NOT used. Please try again in a moment.
_dungeonDoorCopyNote: WO-1114 dungeon door copy. These are the DEFAULTS used when the backend supplies no authored prose for a closed dungeon. THE RULE: a closed dungeon must read as WORLD, never as build status - no build vocabulary is permitted in any value below, and DungeonStatusRegression case [door-copy] enforces that on the parsed values. UNRATIFIED: the owner has an open ruling to accept or rewrite these four pairs (WO-1114 section 9.1).
dungeonSealedBody: Iron and old prayers hold this door. It will not open today.
dungeonCollapsedBody: Rescue crews are still digging through it.
dungeonRescueBody: The Wardens have closed the approach until their people are out.
dungeonFloodedBody: Whatever is down there can wait for the dry season.
_chestCopyNote: WO-1132 loot-chest copy, owner ruling 2026-08-21 ('open chest' / 'not attackable item' / 'can only open outside of combat'). ASCII only (TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu). chestOpenPrompt is the shared Interact-button face when the chest is openable. chestCombatRefusal is shown BOTH as the button face and as the toast on a refused tap - a refused open must never be a dead tap, because a dead tap reads as a bug. It states the WORLD reason (enemies are near), never a system reason, and it is deliberately a standing condition the player can clear by clearing the room: the ruling exists to prevent 'run in, collect and go'. Pinned by BreakableContainerChestRegression case [chest-refusal-has-words], which also enforces the dual-copy law.
_nightMarketNote: WO-1050 THE NIGHT MARKET (2026-08-21) - the store presentation copy. ASCII only. THE RULE THESE SENTENCES ARE WRITTEN TO: the shelf may only advertise what the grant seam actually pays, and no sentence may imply the GAME holds SKR. SKR is Solana Mobile's own governance token - the owner did not mint it, does not own it and is not releasing a token; there is NO in-game SKR ledger, earn loop or spend loop and there must never be one. storeBalance* are a READ-ONLY MIRROR of the players OWN wallet, read through SolanaWalletProvider.GetBalance, never written, never granted, never deducted in-game - which is why the copy says your wallet and never your SKR. The four storeBalance states are deliberately DISTINCT sentences: no wallet connected is NOT the same fact as a zero balance, and neither is an unreadable one. A confident 0 SKR would launder three different facts (genuinely none / SKR mint unprovisioned in this build / the RPC failed) into one number, which is the same defect class that hid keepers-satchel. storeBalanceFiat is APPROXIMATE by construction - it is derived from a live Jupiter quote that moves between render and purchase - so it keeps its tilde and is DROPPED entirely rather than shown stale or invented. storeTrustTreasury names the on-chain Rewards Distributor account and says nothing about what it holds.
storeBandFreeSub: Nothing is asked for before something is given.
storeSpotlightEmpty: Pick a card to see what it holds.
storeBalanceNoWallet: Connect a wallet to see your balance.
storeBalanceUnavailable: Wallet balance unavailable in this build.
storeTrustFee: 0% STORE FEE - EVERY PAYMENT REACHES THE REALM
storeCovenant: You are never required to spend anything. Ever.
_storeBuyGateNote: WO-1121 store BUY GATE, owner rulings 2026-08-21. ASCII only (TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu). Every one of these is a REFUSAL the player can act on - none of them is a dead button and none of them says 'the flag is off'. storeBuyClosed: purchases are not open at all in this build. storeBuyRailNotReady: the flag is on but the payment rail has no resolvable mint, so a tap could not settle - said BEFORE any charge. storeBuyWalletRequired: the price-gated refusal - packs above $4.99 need a connected wallet because a guest save key is device-derived and a lost $49.99 entitlement is a chargeback; {0} is the threshold, formatted from PurchaseGate.WalletRequiredAboveUsd so the sentence can never drift from the constant, and it must keep saying what the player CAN still buy. storeBuyWalletRequiredCta / storeBuyComingSoon are the card's right-rail button faces. These are gated by FeatureFlags.RealmStorePurchase and the wallet rule; the Redeem-a-Code door deliberately is NOT (redeeming spends no money).
storeBuyClosed: Purchases are not open yet. Everything here is still earned in-game.
storeBuyRailNotReady: The payment rail is not ready in this build, so nothing was charged. Try again after the next update.
storeBuyWalletRequired: Packs over {0} need a connected wallet, so what you buy stays yours if you reinstall or change phones. Connect a wallet to buy this one - anything {0} and under you can buy right now.
storeShelfClosed: Coming soon - purchases are not open in this build. Nothing here is required to play.
_raidCooldownNote: WO-728 per-camp raid cooldown. ASCII only (TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu). The owner is red/green colourblind, so EVERY one of these is a WORD the player can read - the card state must never be signalled by tint alone, and a camp on cooldown must SAY so rather than simply not responding to a tap. raidCooldownCardLine {0} and raidCooldownBlocked {0} take the humanised remaining time built from raidDurationHm/raidDurationM/raidDurationSub (RaidStrings.Humanise, which rounds UP so the number the player sees is never optimistic). raidCooldownStarted {0} is the full window length, shown on the victory screen so the wait is announced at the moment it is earned, not discovered later at a refused tap. The DURATIONS themselves are balance and live in RaidCooldownService, not here.
raidCooldownBlocked: This camp is still recovering from your last raid. You can hit it again in {0}.
raidCooldownStarted: The camp is broken for now. It regroups in {0}.
_battleMonthlyNote: WORK_ORDER_battle_and_monthly_packs - the Season Track and Monthly Ledger screens. Keys are named in StoreStrings.SeasonTrackKeys / MonthlyLedgerKeys and NEVER typed inline. Two house rules are load-bearing in this block and both are checkable: (1) the owner is red/green colourblind, so every screen state carries a WORD here - strip every hue and the screens still read; (2) nothing in either family expires, so no sentence here counts down, and the monthly ledger deliberately says 'N claims left' rather than a time.
seasonTrackXpLine: {0} of {1} XP to the next tier
seasonTrackXpLineCapstone: Every tier earned. {0} XP this season.
seasonTrackEarnRate: Battle XP is earned by playing. Every arena battle pays, win or lose, and a win streak pays more. No tier is ever for sale.
seasonTrackKeptForever: What you earn is yours for good. Nothing is taken back when the season ends, and anything you have not claimed is given to you automatically.
seasonTrackNothingToClaim: Nothing to claim yet - play an arena battle.
seasonTrackLaneNotForSale: The premium lane is not on sale in this build. Everything on it is shown to you anyway - you will never be asked to guess what sits behind a lock.
seasonTrackLaneRetro: Unlocking the lane later costs you nothing: every premium reward you already climbed to is handed over at once.
seasonTrackEmpty: No season is running right now. A new one begins on the first of the month.
monthlyLedgerNoCard: You do not hold a ledger. All thirty days are shown below before you ever pay - there is no hidden day and no mystery day.
monthlyLedgerClaimedToday: Claimed. The next one is yours tomorrow.
monthlyLedgerPoolPromise: Miss a day and you lose nothing. A ledger holds thirty claims and lives until every one of them is spent, however long that takes.
monthlyLedgerNoTimer: Nothing here expires, so nothing here counts down.
monthlyLedgerBonusOnly: This is a bonus on top of your free daily reward, never a replacement for it. Claiming one never uses up the other.
monthlyLedgerExclusiveNone: This ledger has no month-exclusive keepsake yet. Nothing is promised here that cannot be shown to you.
monthlyLedgerNotForSale: Ledgers are not on sale in this build. The whole table is on this screen regardless.
monthlyLedgerEmpty: No ledgers are authored right now.
_hudChipCopyNote: WO-1144 HUD chip/face copy, shortened AT SOURCE after the 2026-08-22 headed-fleet capture (break_24_error.png) showed 'Tap to collec' cut mid-word on the Collectors chip and 'Manag...' ellipsised on the Manage bar face. NEITHER was a font bug: the Collectors chip is 220 ref px wide (== EchoUnlockFeedback.EchoChipWidthPx, a fixed rail width three chips share) so its label rect is ~202 ref px, and the action line 'Tap to collect' measures ~214 ref px at the 30 px FontFloor - it could not fit at ANY legible size. The Manage bar face is one sixth of a 46%-wide ActionBar zone, ~144 ref px of label rect, so the WO-1027 session-shape sentence 'Manage - 2 of 3 idle' was about 4x too long for the box it renders in. The fix is SHORTER WORDS HERE, never a smaller font (FontFloor/MinTouchPx are floors, not budget) and never a wider chip (the three rail chips share one right edge). ASCII only - TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu. Pinned by HudLabelFitRegression, which MEASURES each of these strings against its real box using the real font's glyph advances, at both landscape capture aspects.
_invArmoryRailNote: WO-1133 The Armory Rail - every player-facing sentence on the Bag screen, exact text from the ratified design's D9 string table. Flat camelCase keys, matching this file's existing convention. ASCII ONLY - TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu. Both canonical copies (Resources and StreamingAssets) are byte-identical; InventoryArmoryRailRegression asserts the parity, the ASCII rule, AND measures each of these against the real box it renders in using the real font's glyph advances, so a sentence that cannot fit at the legibility floor fails the gate here rather than being cut mid-word on the owner's device. Rail labels are read by HeroInventoryController via InventoryStrings; the rail counts are numbers from the VM, never part of the sentence.
invEmptyWeapons: Nothing here yet. The Market sells blades, and Hollow raiders drop them.
invEmptyArmor: Nothing here yet. The Armorer in town sells plate, and Hollow captains drop it.
invEmptyTrinkets: Nothing here yet. Trinkets come from dungeon chests below the Ember Deep.
invEmptyPotions: Nothing here yet. Brew flasks at the Healer's Cottage, or buy them at the Market.
invEmptySkills: The Knight tree opens here. Ranged, Heal and Sustain, Control.
invEmptyMapLocked: Realm travel is still being built. This section stays visible so it is never a surprise when it opens.
invPaneGearGaps: Two slots are empty. An amulet and a ring are the cheapest points of defence you can add.
invPaneNothingToCompare: There is nothing here to compare yet.
invNextCompareHint: tap another item to compare it
invNextRailHint: the rail keeps every section one tap away
invNextCountHint: sections with items show a count on the rail
invVerdictBetter: Better than what you are carrying.
invVerdictWorse: Worse than what you are carrying.
invVerdictWearing: This is what you are carrying now.
